Joey · User Guide

Everything you need to
get started.

Joey is designed to stay out of your way. This guide walks you through the main features — from saving your first article to exporting your full library.

Version 1.0.0

01Saving an article

Click the Joey icon.
The rest is automatic.

When you're on a page you want to read later, click the Joey icon in your browser toolbar. A popup appears showing the article title and URL. Hit Save Article and it's instantly added to your list.

By default, articles are saved in Reader View — Joey extracts the main content and strips away ads, navigation, and other clutter, giving you a clean reading experience. Before saving, you have a few options:

  • Add tags — type or pick from your existing list; tags are applied on save
  • Download full page to hard disk — saves a complete .html snapshot to your computer, images included
  • Text only — saves the article text without images, keeping things lightweight
📖

About Reader View and images: how images are preserved in Reader View can vary depending on the site and your browser settings. If the result doesn't look right, delete the article and re-save it with Text only checked instead.

💡

Already saved the article? Click Open Reading List at the bottom of the popup to jump straight to your library.

The Joey popup — click the toolbar icon on any article page

Click image to enlarge

02Your library

Everything you've saved,
in one place.

The reading list shows your saved articles as a visual card grid — thumbnail, title, source, tags, and estimated reading time at a glance. The left sidebar lets you switch between My List, Archive, and Favourites.

  • Click any card to open the article in the built-in reader
  • Switch between grid and list layout using the toggle in the top bar
  • Toggle light or dark mode with the appearance button
  • Article count is shown next to each section in the sidebar

My List — your saved articles at a glance

Click image to enlarge

03Reader & highlights

Read deeply.
Note what matters.

Click any article to open it in the built-in reader — a clean, distraction-free view that strips away ads, sidebars, and clutter. Select any passage of text to highlight it; a small toolbar lets you pick a colour and optionally attach a note.

All highlights appear in the Annotations panel on the right. Click Jump to on any annotation to scroll straight back to that passage.

  • Select text → choose a highlight colour → optionally add a note
  • Annotations panel lists all highlights with jump links
  • Use Read Aloud in the top bar to have the article read to you — adjust speed with the – and + controls next to it
  • Export the article to Markdown or JSON from the top bar — highlights and notes included
🔊

Read Aloud works on any saved article and is great for commuting or resting your eyes. It starts reading from the current scroll position and adjusts to your chosen playback speed.

Reader view — highlights in text, annotations in the side panel

Click image to enlarge

04Tags & organisation

Tag once, filter forever.

Hover over any article card to reveal its action bar. From there you can star it as a favourite, archive it, edit the title, or add and remove tags. Tags appear in the left sidebar and let you filter your entire list instantly with one click.

  • Hover a card to reveal quick actions — favourite, archive, edit, tag, delete
  • Click any tag in the sidebar to filter the list to matching articles
  • An article can have multiple tags
  • Tags are included when you export your library

Sidebar tags — click to filter

Card actions — hover to reveal

05Bulk actions

Manage many articles at once.

Hover over a card and check the checkbox that appears in its corner to enter selection mode. Select as many articles as you like — a toolbar appears at the top of the list with all available bulk actions.

  • Select individual cards by hovering and checking the corner checkbox
  • Use Select all to grab everything in the current view
  • Bulk actions: Archive, Favourite, Export MD, Delete
  • Press Cancel or click away to exit selection mode

Select multiple articles and act on all of them at once

Click image to enlarge

06Search

Find anything, instantly.

The search bar in the top-right searches across titles and sources as you type. For more precise results, wrap a phrase in quotes to match it exactly — useful when you remember a specific wording from an article you saved.

  • Type freely to search by keyword across title and source
  • Use "quotes" for exact phrase matching
  • Switch between grid and list layout using the view toggle
  • Toggle light and dark mode with the appearance button

Search bar, layout toggle, and light/dark switch

Click image to enlarge

07Export & import

Your data,
your format.

Joey's export panel lives at the bottom of the left sidebar. You can export your entire library or individual articles — tags, highlights, and notes are always included. Supported formats are Markdown and JSON.

  • Export all (Markdown) — human-readable, works with most note apps
  • Export all (JSON) — complete data, ideal for backups and migration
  • Import (.md file) — restore a previous Markdown export
  • Import (JSON) — restore a full JSON backup
  • Check integrity — scans for duplicate or empty articles
💡

Individual articles can also be exported from inside the reader using the Export to Markdown and Export to JSON buttons in the top bar.

Export / import panel — bottom of the left sidebar

Click image to enlarge

💾

Back up regularly. Joey stores everything locally in your browser. Use Export all (JSON) frequently and save the file to a cloud service you trust — Google Drive, Dropbox, iCloud, or any synced folder. This is the only safeguard against data loss if you reset your browser or switch devices.
